assessments.reasoning: The License Index’s SCOPE.md at commit cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 admits historical editions and instruments covering software and relevant documentation. Its license criterion at bytes [533,942) applies because W3C identifies an edition and supplies an operative grant. The word “Notice” in the Index name does not reduce the instrument to a notice.

Both captures come from https://www.w3.org/copyright/software-license-2002/ and cover [0,16384) and [16384,28021) of one English HTML witness. Both report SHA-256 b297963744c1fd2561233e56cddafaf1c4f6584a3ce59558b0221c2951b8f244. The page heading reads “Software and Document license - 2002 version”. The License section grants permission to copy, modify and distribute software and its documentation subject to conditions. The Versions and Changes sections identify this dated route as W3C’s notice and license and state when it became active. Together they explain the Index’s edition-specific name.

The Index decision at commit afb962e68831a16accb80c70159b1e2f1fbb4dbc, bytes [5976,6183), records permanent ID 3edf5b8afb07494db11085f06ddc6492, W3C Software Notice and License (2002 edition), edition `w3c-2002`, revision `sha256:b297963744c1fd2561233e56cddafaf1c4f6584a3ce59558b0221c2951b8f244`, kind `license` and lifecycle `active`. The ID matches the claim subject after its `e-` prefix. The neighboring 1998 and 2015 rows have distinct IDs and revisions. Their shared `active` value does not identify the edition.

challenge.method: Tested the hypothesis that the archive banner requires an Index lifecycle of `historical`. Compared the page heading, grant, version links and change history with the Index rows for the 1998, 2002 and 2015 editions. Checked the separate 2002 document-license and short-notice links as possible mistaken specimens.
challenge.results: The publisher’s “This version” link identifies the 2002 software-license route. Its change history distinguishes the 1998 predecessor, including removal of the ownership notice and ambiguous grant of “use”. The short notice, document license, moving latest-version link and 2015 revision each have a different role or route. The archive banner establishes a change in W3C practice. The exact 2002 Index row expressly assigns `active`, resolving the proposed lifecycle conflict.

limitations: W3C reports that the license applied to software it published before May 13, 2015. On that date it adopted a revised and renamed license and applied it to all W3C documents previously available under the 2002 license. W3C says the new license grants all permissions granted under the 2002 license.

The grant addresses the covered software and associated documentation, subject to notice conditions. Project-specific use, rights to redistribute the license text, and installation eligibility require separate evidence.

The Index lifecycle concerns documentary lookup. Publisher currency, SPDX deprecation and release authorization are separate determinations. The archive’s links to FSF and OSI describe the publisher’s rationale for its drafting and supply no independent assessment here.
reasoning: W3C’s versioned English page identifies the 2002 formulation of its software notice and license, gives its conditional grant and explicitly dates activation to December 31, 2002. The Index names that exact witness W3C Software Notice and License (2002 edition) and assigns it `active`. W3C’s subsequent adoption of revised terms and the Index’s continued maintenance of this reference are compatible.
